title: Wait for a promise
summary: An async test can await a promise. resolves checks the value with which it finishes successfully.
introduction: An async test can await a promise. resolves checks the value with which it finishes successfully. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: An async test can await a promise. resolves checks the value with which it finishes successfully.

blocks.code:
import { test, expect, jest, beforeEach } from "@jest/globals";
test("loads a score", async () => { await expect(Promise.resolve(8)).resolves.toBe(8); });
blocks.title: Wait for a promise

blocks.text: The test waits and then passes because the resolved value is 8.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Use Promise.resolve(9) and update the expected result.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Forgetting await or return can let an async test finish too early.
For more detail later, use this [Jest further reading](https://jestjs.io/docs/getting-started).
